title: 2017's Interstellar Object Sped Up. Why? #shorts
description:
In 2017, ʻOumuamua became the first object confirmed to come from interstellar space. As it left the Sun, it sped up slightly, like a comet releasing gas, but it showed no visible cloud and no tail. In 2023, scientists suggested in Nature that hydrogen, made by cosmic rays in its ice and released when it warmed up, gave it a gentle push. Verdict: best guess. It's long gone, so we can't check.

Five more solar system mysteries are in the full video on the channel.

Images: ʻOumuamua seen by the William Herschel Telescope, A. Fitzsimmons (QUB), public domain; artist's impression ESO/M. Kornmesser (derivative: nagualdesign), CC BY-SA 4.0. 3D scenes are illustrations.
Sources: Bergner & Seligman, Nature (2023), arXiv:2303.13698; Wikipedia, "1I/ʻOumuamua"
